bull_bear.body: Expansion funded by internal accruals + balance-sheet cash for FY27; no QIP needed near-term; debt is first preference if external funds required (healthy D/E). Prepaying vendors aggressively (creditor days down ~10 days) to be "best paymaster" / priority vendor — can pause prepayment program to free cash for store rollout. Targets: inventory 90-100 days, creditors 45 days. Operating cash flow guided positive in FY27 even after 175-200 store openings.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Inventory:** Elevated March inventory from safety-stock build (geopolitics); >1-yr-old <5%, >6-month <24% (so 76% <6mo, ~50% <3mo). ~15% of season inventory carried to next season (reprocessed, not disposed).
- **Demand:** May FY27 saw slight slowdown (war impact); April good, June expected biggest month. Tier-2/3 relatively insulated.
- **Competition / margin:** Peers may absorb cost inflation; V2 passing on fully — execution risk on volume if pricing bites.
- **New-store execution:** Historical "wrong location" rate fell from 10-12% (4 yrs ago) to 2-3% now; of 22 stores once flagged for closure, 21 turned profitable, only 1 shut.
- **Key-man:** CEO is sole face; mgmt says 6+ leaders (10+ yr tenure) could field calls; data-driven culture cited as mitigant.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident, long-term framed ("20-year vision", "blue ocean"), data-driven, disciplined. Repeatedly conditions aggressive guidance on "continued momentum/performance." Candid on near-term May softness and one-offs.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- SSSG % optically "underpowered" in Q4 (7.74%) only due to high base (PSF ~Rs.1,040 vs peers ~40-50% lower base); old-store PSF still grew ~8.5%. Company-level PSF declined ~7-8% purely from new-store area dilution, not weakness.
- Reported (Ind-AS) EBITDA margin (13.7% Q4 / 14.9% FY) materially higher than pre-Ind-AS (6.8% Q4 / 9.0% FY) — lease accounting gap; mgmt manages business on pre-Ind-AS. Changed lease accounting policy last quarter (assess new store over 2-3 yrs) to narrow Ind-AS vs pre-Ind-AS gap.
- Operating leverage at consol level structurally suppressed until new-area addition slows (~2,000 stores) — blended margin flat by design despite improving old-store economics.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Total equity rose to Rs 902 Cr in FY2026 from Rs 346 Cr in FY2025, with other equity at Rs 866 Cr versus Rs 312 Cr, alongside net cash from financing activities of +Rs 319 Cr in FY2026 (against outflows in the prior two years).
- Inventories nearly doubled to Rs 1,142 Cr in FY2026 from Rs 558 Cr in FY2025, driving a working-capital change of -Rs 549 Cr and negative net cash from operating activities of -Rs 103 Cr in FY2026 versus +Rs 201 Cr in FY2025.
- Debt remains modest relative to equity: current borrowings Rs 230 Cr and non-current borrowings Rs 24 Cr in FY2026, with trade payables of Rs 463 Cr; total assets Rs 2,422 Cr.
- The deck makes no mention of any dividend, buyback or stated payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Category mix:** Men's ~41-42%, Women's ~27%, Kids ~25% (rest GM). Highest-growth categories: kurtis, men's woven pajamas, men's casual shirts.
- **Geographies:** Present in 25 states. Strong/performing: Gujarat, Karnataka (~15-20 stores), West Bengal (~15 stores), Andhra, Goa, Maharashtra. Newly entered (9 states): AP, Telangana, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, etc. Goal: every state in India.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries

business.body:
- Mission stated as "to democratize fashion by offering high-quality, trendy apparel at affordable prices to value conscious consumers across all tiers of cities", with the motto "Value & Variety"; deck header reads "Leading the way in Affordable, High Quality Fashion".
- Primarily operates in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, running V2 Retail stores offering apparel and general merchandise for the entire family, serving India's "neo middle class" and "middle class".
- Founded 2001 by Mr. Ram Chandra Agarwal (described as "the pioneer in value retailing" in India); listed 2007; the 'Vishal' brand was sold in 2011 due to operational losses and the company was renamed V2 Retail Limited.
- Demand framed around occasions (festivals, weddings, social functions), functional needs (discount/offers/replacement) and emotional needs (new seasons/trends), with brand recall driven by price, quality of make, fabric, durability, comfort and fit.
- Promoter-family-led board: Chairman & MD Ram Chandra Agarwal (~30 years), Whole Time Directors Uma Agarwal (~15 years, marketing) and Akash Agarwal (10+ years; e-commerce, procurement and finance).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Reporting basis] The deck presents two parallel sets of consolidated financials - post-Ind AS and "Pre Ind AS" - which differ materially at the EBITDA level (FY26 EBIDTA Rs 455 Cr / 14.9% margin post-Ind AS versus Rs 277 Cr / 9.0% pre-Ind AS), because leases sit in EBITDA under the pre-Ind AS view; comparisons must specify which basis is used.
- [Exceptional item] FY2026 profit before tax of Rs 215 Cr includes an exceptional gain of Rs 27.7 Cr; profit before tax and exceptional items was Rs 187 Cr.
- [Disclosure gap] Several operating charts (Rent per Sq. Ft., Sales per Sq. Ft. trend, Store Count, Retail Space, Inventory/Creditors/NWC days, ROE) appear as slide titles only - the underlying data labels did not survive extraction, so those series cannot be asserted.
- [Marketing] Multiple slides are dedicated to "Media & Promotion Campaigns", "Select New Stores Opening" and "Store Experience", but they are image-only in the extract with no accompanying text or spend disclosure.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Gross margin 30.3% Q4 pre-Ind-AS (+270 bps YoY): driven by less winter discounting, better product mix, inter-store transfers, higher full-price share (89-90%).
- Yarn/cotton cost inflation (3-4%, geopolitics-driven) to be fully passed on via MRP increase (~Rs. 10-12 on Rs. 300 ASP); will NOT absorb in margin (contrast with peers who plan partial absorption). Gross margin to stay 28-30%.
- Three margin levers (offset by new-area dilution): (1) fabric nomination/centralization — only ~20% nominated now, potential 3-5% saving; (2) per-sqft opex reduction Rs. 200→190→target 175; (3) SSSG. Old-store EBITDA ~11-12% vs new-store ~5-6%.
- Marketing spend ~0.3% of sales FY26; FY27 <0.5%, mostly for new stores.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Rev Rs. 797 cr (+60% YoY); reported EBITDA 13.7%, pre-Ind-AS EBITDA 6.8%; PAT Rs. 17.5 cr reported / Rs. 25 cr pre-Ind-AS; SSSG 7.74%; net +33 stores in qtr → 325 (FY net +136); ~3.5 mn sq ft. FY26: Rev Rs. 3,067 cr (+63%), PAT Rs. 162 cr (+125%), ROE 26%. Guidance: ~50% rev growth 2 yrs, SSSG 8-10%, 170-200 stores FY27, PSF/margins flat near-term. One-offs: Rs. 5.77 cr asset write-off, Rs. 6-7 cr deprec accounting change, safety-stock inventory build.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Revenue:** at least 50% YoY growth for the next 2 years (conditional on continued momentum/performance).
- **SSSG:** 8%-10% guided going forward (FY26 delivered ~8.6%).
- **Store additions:** FY27 target 170-200 stores (mgmt also said "at least 170-180"); ~50-60% new area added per year. Aspiration: ~500 stores end-FY27, ~250 adds the year after; long-term ceiling of 2,500 V2 stores in India.
- **Revenue/sqft (PSF):** Company-level PSF held ~flat near-term (blended) because of heavy new-area dilution; long-term target Rs. 1,200/sqft at company level. New stores open at ~70% of old-store PSF (Rs. 700-750), breakeven ~Rs. 500/sqft.
- **Margin:** Maintain similar EBITDA margins in FY27 (reported ~13-15%; pre-Ind-AS standalone ~9.4%). Gross margin guided 28%-30%. Operating leverage at consol level deferred until new-area addition slows (~when reaching 2,000 stores).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body: FY27: 170-200 new stores (60 planned to open in Q1 FY27 alone). Robust pipeline; enters new state with 4-5 stores, gathers data via 70-80 metric location scorecard, then scales by state performance. ~30-40% of new stores in newer regions, 50-60% in core strong regions.
outlook.title: Pipeline (store rollout)

outlook.body:
- Store expansion is the core growth engine (2,500-store TAM in India). No new format/vertical until 2,500 V2 stores reached (explicitly declined Trends-style multi-brand). No overseas expansion. Moved away from in-house manufacturing — now retail-only.
- Customer engagement: no formal loyalty program but 8-crore customer database reached via WhatsApp/RCS/SMS with vouchers/gifts. Word-of-mouth + product is primary marketing.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Aggressive, data-driven value-fashion store rollout in tier-2/3 and rural India — guiding ~50% revenue growth for the next 2 years funded by internal accruals — with stable EBITDA margins because heavy new-area addition (50-60%/yr) keeps blended company PSF flat even as old-store economics improve.

open.item: The FY 2026-27 store-opening plan alone is 170-200 stores, taking the network towards 500 stores.
In FY 2026-27, around 30-40% of new stores are planned to come from newer regions (e.g. Karnataka, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Maharashtra), with the rest in core markets.
FY 2026-27's planned 170-200 new stores are expected to be fully fundable from internal accruals and cash on the books, following the Rs.400 crore QIP.
FY 2026-27 plan is to open 170-200 new stores, taking the network towards approximately 500 stores, with each new site cleared through a 70-point scorecard before a lease is signed.
Around 50-60% of FY 2026-27 new stores are planned to deepen presence in regions V2 already operates in, with the remaining 30-40% extending into newer territory.
Management guided gross margin to stay within a 28-30% band as the network scales.
Working capital, deliberately stretched in March 2026 for safety stock, is expected to return to its normal shape across FY27 at 90-100 days of inventory and creditors near 45 days.
In-house merchandising and fleet-management software is planned for full deployment in FY 2026-27, alongside expanded AI agent coverage across buying decisions.
Management will not consider adjacent formats or categories before reaching at least 2,500 V2 stores, choosing to focus on capturing the existing value-fashion opportunity first.
Management expects to work back inventory days to 90-100 days and creditor days to around 45 days as new stores absorb the current elevated safety-stock build.
Company is developing its own merchandising and fleet-management platforms, in addition to existing AI-agent use in article creation and supplier workflows.
V2 has set a single target of 2,500 stores, with no new formats or adjacent ventures to be pursued until this count is reached.
Of the Rs.400 crore QIP raised, about Rs.135 crore has been used to repay existing debt while roughly Rs.165 crore is earmarked for the retail rollout, supply-chain capability and digital systems.

open.item: Management flags that fast store openings strain site selection, staffing and consistency, and responds with a 70-point scorecard per location and a new-state playbook of 4-5 probe stores before scaling (3 closures were recorded against 139 openings in FY26).
Supply-chain resilience is being built around a centralised Gurgaon distribution centre, an owned fleet, safety-stock judgment, and in-house fleet-management software currently under development.

risks.note: The Directors' Report states that 'the operating environment for the retail industry continued to remain challenging during the year' and that the Company delivered results 'despite these headwinds', indicating the business remains exposed to cyclical/macro pressure on Indian retail demand even as it posted strong growth.

The Company's own history ('The Journey') records that its predecessor, Vishal Retail, pursued debt-funded over-expansion that met the 2008-09 downturn, forcing divestiture of the Vishal retail business and brand and a relaunch as V2 Retail from a much smaller base -- a structural precedent relevant given the current pace of aggressive store rollout (136 net stores added in FY26 alone, versus 97 stores built over the prior decade).
risks.risk: History of expansion-led financial distress in the same corporate entity

risks.note: The store network's stated anchor remains Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha and the Eastern heartland (which individually carry the largest store counts, e.g. 54 in Uttar Pradesh and 49 in Bihar), with Western and Southern states (Maharashtra, Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Southern states) described as only recently turning 'from experiments into proven territory', implying continued reliance on a geographically concentrated base.
risks.risk: Geographic concentration in Northern and Eastern India
